{enedwaith_clan_moot}The Clanmoot 
{enedwaith_clan_moot_desc}DO NOT TRANSLATE
{enedwaith_clan_moot_desc_short}DO NOT TRANSLATE
{enedwaith_clan_moot_northern_european}The Clanmoot 
{enedwaith_clan_moot_northern_european_desc}Enedwaith is a land of many clans- each with their own unique quirks. Some are farmers, fishers, hunters, and warriors. And their origins are diverse- whether they date from the despoiling of the Great Forest, the years after the Last Alliance, or even from the impacts of Wulf's conquest. When the situation calls for it, as it has often of late, the clans come together within the Clanmoot to debate and decide upon a cause the clans should take together. Violence is forbidden within the hall, and those who break this rule without due justification will face the justice of the Dubhsìthe, who often execute those who break this one precept. It is as close to a center of goverment as the clans possess, and is guarded when not in use by the Mocháini. It is also here that the Speaker of the Moot, the individual elected to enact the will of the Clanmoot, formally sits, regardless of their clan of origin. The hall itself is also said to have been constructed after the War of the Last Alliance as a replacement for the lost Tír Croícoill of Athámor which served the same purpose prior to the despoiling of the Great Forest.\n\nWithin the hall, the plans to reclaim the shattered clanseats and the Dunland heartlands were discussed, with the regions being:\nLugiu, Maolfinn, Angren Bay, Maolrunaidh, Heorotscir, Larfearann, Caladir, Eryn Vorn, Cairill, Saralainn, Dunland Lowlands, Dunland Border and Dunland Proper.
{enedwaith_clan_moot_northern_european_desc_short}Large hall where the clans of Enedwaith meet.
{enedwaith_clan_moot_mesoamerican}The Clanmoot
{enedwaith_clan_moot_mesoamerican_desc}Enedwaith is a land of many clans- each with their own unique quirks. Some are farmers, fishers, hunters, and warriors. And their origins are diverse- whether they date from the despoiling of the Great Forest, the years after the Last Alliance, or even from the impacts of Wulf's conquest. When the situation calls for it, as it has often of late, the clans come together within the Clanmoot to debate and decide upon a cause the clans should take together. Violence is forbidden within the hall, and those who break this rule without due justification will face the justice of the Dubhsìthe, who often execute those who break this one precept. It is as close to a center of goverment as the clans possess, and is guarded when not in use by the Mocháini. It is also here that the Speaker of the Moot, the individual elected to enact the will of the Clanmoot, formally sits, regardless of their clan of origin. The hall itself is also said to have been constructed after the War of the Last Alliance as a replacement for the lost Tír Croícoill of Athámor which served the same purpose prior to the despoiling of the Great Forest.\n\nWithin the hall, the plans to reclaim the shattered clanseats and the Dunland heartlands were discussed, with the regions of those clanseats being:\nLugiu, Maolfinn, Angren Bay, Maolrunaidh, Heorotscir, Larfearann, Caladir, Eryn Vorn, Dunland Lowlands, Dunland Border and Dunland Proper.
{enedwaith_clan_moot_mesoamerican_desc_short}Large hall where the clans of Enedwaith meet.

{enedwaith_moot_muster}Clanmoot Muster Ground 
{enedwaith_moot_muster_desc}DO NOT TRANSLATE
{enedwaith_moot_muster_desc_short}DO NOT TRANSLATE
{enedwaith_moot_muster_northern_european}Clanmoot Muster Ground 
{enedwaith_moot_muster_northern_european_desc}With the reclaimation of the clanseats underway, the Clanmoot decided that a centralized system of military recruitment for Enedwaith must be established alongside the traditional levy system that has served well in the past. This mustering ground is one such facility, training and arming the professional military of each clan, in contrast to the non-professional levy units that are mustered from industries and economic centers. This allows the professional, elite soldiers of each clan to be trained and replenished away from their ancestral heartland once their clanseat has been reclaimed, allowing each clan to fully dedicate resources and troops, instead of focusing on the reclaimation of their clanseat. These structures are a great boon for the clans, allowing them to match their foes. 
{enedwaith_moot_muster_northern_european_desc_short}Mustering grounds where the professional elites of each clan may be trained and replenished. 
¬--------------
{enedwaith_moot_barracks}Clanmoot Barracks 
{enedwaith_moot_barracks_desc}DO NOT TRANSLATE
{enedwaith_moot_barracks_desc_short}DO NOT TRANSLATE
{enedwaith_moot_barracks_northern_european}Clanmoot Barracks 
{enedwaith_moot_barracks_northern_european_desc}With the Declaration of Athámor, and the establishment of the Ruling Council, their first step was to establish a formal military that would act as a symbol of this new era. This large barracks acts as a center of this recruitment, retaining the word Clanmoot as both a tribute to the old ruling council, and because it became a synonym for these centralized centers of recruitment. Acting as an extension of the Clan Heralds, allowing anyone with a love for the Confederacy of Athámor to enlist, this force is able to match some of the best troops that the Confederacy's neighbours can field- no longer should they be dismissed as clansmen, for now they are a true nation, that can meet any other on equal grounds, whether it be in peace or war.\n\nAdditionally, this barracks also allows for higher quality weapons to be supplied to troops thanks to the skilled Mocháini and Liadan blacksmiths that reside within.
{enedwaith_moot_barracks_northern_european_desc_short}Large barracks that musters Enedwaith's elite troops and provides higher levels of armour.

{barrow_downs_northern_european_desc}These haunted crypts were once a sacred Númenórean burial site in the Northern kingdom of Cardolan. Cursed by the Witch-king of Angmar, the halls are now inhabited by evil wights who prey upon any who dare trespass upon the ancient mounds. Those who live near the barrows find it difficult to feel safe with such an evil presence nearby. However, if the wights that spawn from the crypts are slain, people will feel more secure living nearby and as wights are slain, people will be begin to inhabit these lands once more.

{pass_hold}pass_hold
{pass_hold_desc}DO NOT TRANSLATE
{pass_hold_desc_short}DO NOT TRANSLATE
{pass_hold_northern_european}Mountain Hold
{pass_hold_northern_european_desc}The Anduin Vale is now prosperous. The goblins have been driven from the passes and now there is one final step to take to ensure the security of those who travel them. The wooden keeps shall be converted into stone holds, and likewise as the keeps are improved so shall the main passes. While the smaller passes and trails will always be fraught with perils of nature, the main passes shall be made navigable for study wagons that shall bring more trade to the Vale. The stone holds shall be able to shelter these wagons and any number of travellers. Some men now even boast that the security of the passes will allow even the most old and infirm to make the trip in peace. Most of all, the veterans of this terrible guerrilla war fought in the mountains to hold the passes open, freed from their duty, can now be raised in the defence of the Vale of the Anduin itself. Experienced and equipped, they now march to serve the Vale wherever they are required.

{council_chambers_southern_european_desc_short}A Miners Quarters helps the survivability of any settlement and increases public order.
{council_chambers_gondor}Governor's Quarters
{council_chambers_gondor_desc}As a settlement grows in size, it tends to be seen as the hub of a variety of local districts, each of which will either be run by land owners, or the men appointed to govern the district in the Steward's name. These men regularly gather together in the Governor's Quarters, to ensure the parts of a region work together as a whole, and that issues facing the region are made apparent to the nobles of Minas Tirith.
{council_chambers_gondor_desc_short}A Governor's Quarters helps the survivability of any settlement and increases public order.

{city_hall_mesoamerican}Steward's Hall

Though its primary role is still to serve as a court of law and to collect tax, if it didn’t provide a home to the settlement's various civil departments, the entire place would probably degenerate into fetid squalor. The hall also provides ample stores for the recruitment of more troops and helps to lower construction costs as the various Fieflords meet to discuss matters of high importance to the sons of Númenor.

{city_hall_greek}Hall of Culture

{mayors_palace_northern_european}Royal Hall
{mayors_palace_northern_european_desc}Once a settlement reaches a power base rivalling the very capital, then there is a very real chance that the King, Regent or Councilmaster will visit the town to discuss issues regarding the entire realm. It is therefore only necessary to construct a Royal Hall in which to accommodate him. This majestic structure also attracts many more Lords and Nobles and the issues concerning the settlement itself are dealt with expertly and its day-to-day running begins to work like clockwork, with improvements across the board.
{mayors_palace_northern_european_desc_short}A Royal Hall does wonders to help the survivability of any settlement and increases public order considerably.
{mayors_palace_mesoamerican}Royal Hall
{mayors_palace_mesoamerican_desc}The Royal Hall represents the final frontier in terms of ensuring that the people of a great settlement don’t forget just who is in charge. Though the Palace is where the Fieflord of the region resides, the building is actually the property of the High King and is built to ensure governance of the settlement is handled expertly, with many rooms for storage, a large meeting chamber for Fieflords and Nobles to discuss matters concerning the realm and its interests. This majestic structure also attracts many more Lords and Nobles and the issues concerning the settlement itself are dealt with expertly and its day-to-day running begins to work like clockwork, with improvements across the board. This majestic structure also attracts many more Lords and Nobles and the issues concerning the settlement itself are dealt with expertly and its day-to-day running begins to work like clockwork, with improvements across the board.
{mayors_palace_middle_eastern_desc_short}A High Palace does wonders to help the survivability of any settlement and increases public order considerably.
{mayors_palace_eastern_european}Chieftain's Hall
{mayors_palace_eastern_european_desc}Once a settlement grows to rival the power of Barad-dûr, Orthanc or Goblin-town, then the decision is passed to construct a Chieftain's Hall to house the more powerful and skilful Orc Chieftain's. This grand structure also doubles as an enormous barracks for the hordes of slaves captured by the followers or Melkor and these slaves are constantly set to work helping to maintain order, construct buildings cheaply or to outfit Orc warriors. Should the High Chieftain or one of the Úlairi pass through, then they also have a place to stay.
{mayors_palace_eastern_european_desc_short}The Chieftain's Hall does wonders to help the survivability of any settlement and increases public order considerably.
{mayors_palace_greek}Valian Council Hall
{mayors_palace_greek_desc}It is rare to see such large settlements of the Elves in the Third Age as many of their people sail westward but, should a settlement grow to rival Mithlond, Imladris or Caras Galadhon then a Valian Council Hall will likely be constructed to maintain peace throughout the realm. Built on the site of the Hall of Culture, the Valian Council Hall takes its name from the shrine to the Valar constructed in the centre of the structure. From this almost 'holy' meeting point, the great Lords of the Elves meet to discuss all aspects of Elven life and the result is improvements for the settlement in all areas; greater troop recruitment, improved stores to provide for more units, lower construction costs and greater peace in the settlement.
{mayors_palace_greek_desc_short}A Valian Council Hall does wonders to help the survivability of any settlement and increases public order considerably.
{mayors_palace_southern_european}Great Miners Hall
{mayors_palace_southern_european_desc}With the mines at full capacity and the Union members and Lords of the settlement working together, the decision is passed to construct a Great Miners Hall. This large structure serves as a barracks for the many miners, a meeting hall for the ancient art of smoking and as a great council chamber. The increased capacity for Lords and miners allows the allocation of labour far more easily and the Hall brings with it great improvements throughout the settlement. Not to pass up tradition, the Hall also features a room found in all Great Dwarven settlements, 'Aulë's Chamber'. The chamber features a large heptagonal table with 7 large seats, its only purpose is to be ready to provide space for a meeting of the 7 clans should the need ever arise.
{mayors_palace_southern_european_desc_short}A Great Miners Hall does wonders to help the survivability of any settlement and increases public order considerably.

Lastly, it is also a beacon of hope, built as a hall grand enough to house a king; should one ever sit on the ancient throne at Minas Tirith.

{c_logging_house}Logging House
{c_logging_house_desc}A Logging House is a structure where timber is stored after being cut down in nearby forest. This building will help greatly in allowing for faster logging which in turn would allow us to use more wood to equip our soldiers. However, the basic design of the structure makes it quite limited in use but can be further upgraded to a Sawmill to provide increasingly good benefits. Can only be built in Fangorn Camp.
{c_logging_house_desc_short}A Logging House is a structure to aid in the storage of timber.
{c_sawmill}Sawmill
{c_sawmill_desc}A Sawmill is a building where timber is stored and processed so it can be used for other works like for buildings and parts of armour for units. This increased efficiency of manufacture of wood through higher rates of logging allows the armies to grow faster and to be re-fitted with new equipment after battles. This structure can be upgraded further into a Lumber Yard. Can only be built in Fangorn Camp.
{c_sawmill_desc_short}A Sawmill is a structure which will aid in the processing of wood.
{c_lumber_yard}Lumber Yard
{c_lumber_yard_desc}A Lumber Yard is a place where timber is stored and processed for the use in buildings and armour. The advanced structure of the buildings allows it to process wood very quickly meaning even more workers can be sent to cut down the wood in the nearby forests. This refined process will greatly boost the replenish rate of the armies as well as reducing the cost of wooden buildings. Can only be built in Fangorn Camp.
{c_lumber_yard_desc_short}A Lumber Yard is a building which will store and process wood.

These strong beasts are only found in the jungles of Far Harad, a long distance from Umbar and Gondor. Systems need to be put in place to transport these creatures far north to the battlefields of Middle-earth. Stops need to be made to feed them and to provide water to them, guards are needed in-case bandits attempt to let the Mûmakil loose, and roads need to be maintained the entire way. It is worth it however, for these mobile fortresses are both respected and feared throughout Middle-earth and are the mightiest weapon in all of Harad.

{great_gates_northern_european}The Great Gates
{great_gates_northern_european_desc}The Great Gate is the main gate on the first level of the City. It is in the City Wall - or Othram - facing eastward across the Pelennor Fields toward the Anduin. \n\nIn front of the Great Gate there is a large paved area called the Gateway. The roads to Minas Tirith meet here, including the North-way that joins the Great West Road to Rohan, the South Road to the southern provinces of Gondor, and the road to Osgiliath. \n\nThe Great Gate is made of iron and steel guarded by stone towers and bastions. {ecthelion_northern_european}The Tower of Ecthelion
{ecthelion_northern_european_desc}The White Tower of Minas Tirith. The Tower of Ecthelion is 50 fathoms (300 feet) tall. The plain white standard of the Stewards of Gondor flows from its pinnacle. The Tower stands in the centre of the Citadel on the seventh level of the city. In front of the Tower is the Court of the Fountain where the White Tree of Gondor grew. \n\nIn the Tower Hall is the throne of the King of Gondor upon a dais, and at the foot the dais on the lowest step is a black chair where the Steward of Gondor sits. There is a chamber high in the Tower and above it in the summit there is a secret room where the palantír of Minas Anor called the Anor-stone is kept. \n\nThe White Tower was first built by King Calimehtar in 1900 in order to house the palantír. In 2698, the Tower was repaired and rebuilt by the Steward Ecthelion I, for whom the Tower came to be named. \n\nThe elite military unit in Minas Tirith is called the Guard of the Citadel or the Guard of the Tower of Gondor.
{ecthelion_northern_european_desc_short}The Tower of Ecthelion is overlooking Minas Tirith and bears the standard of the city.

{orthanc}orthanc_tower

{orthanc_desc_short}DO NOT TRANSLATE
{orthanc_northern_european}The Orthanc
{orthanc_northern_european_desc}Within the Ring of Isengard is a large circular plain. The ground dips slightly to form a shallow bowl, at the centre of which stands the Tower of Orthanc. Orthanc was made of hard, gleaming black stone. The Tower was man-made but appeared like a great spur of rock thrusting out of the plain. \n\nIt is composed of four, many-sided columns of rock joined together that rose to a height of 500 feet and then fork into four sharp pinnacles. Between the pinnacles is a small roof of polished stone carved with astronomical signs where a person can stand and watch the stars. This platform can be reached by a single staircase of many thousand steps inside the Tower. \n\nThe only door into Orthanc is on the eastern side, in the angle of two of the stone columns. The Keys of Orthanc are used to lock this door. A flight of 27 stone steps leads up to the door. Above the door is a balcony with an iron railing, and a shuttered window opened onto the balcony. There are many more tall windows around the Tower of Orthanc, even in the four pinnacles.
{orthanc_northern_european_desc_short}The central tower of Isengard.

{dragon_inn}dragon_inn
{dragon_inn_desc}DO NOT TRANSLATE
{dragon_inn_desc_short}DO NOT TRANSLATE
{dragon_inn_northern_european}The Green Dragon
{dragon_inn_northern_european_desc}The Green Dragon is the last building on the side of Bywater nearest to Hobbiton. It is located on the Bywater Road which links with the Great East Road. Hobbits from Bywater, Hobbiton, and the surrounding area come to the Green Dragon for pints of beer and gossip. \n\nOn April 27, 2941, at the beginning of the quest to the Lonely Mountain, Thorin and Company went ahead to the Green Dragon to make preparations and await Bilbo Baggins. \n\nOne evening in early April of 3018, Sam Gamgee and Ted Sandyman, the miller's son, were at the Green Dragon. Sam spoke of strange things that had been happening, such as queer folk passing through the Shire and the Tree-man his cousin Hal claimed to have seen on the North Moors. Sam was particularly sad about the passing of the Elves westward as they left Middle-earth. Ted Sandyman scoffed at Sam's tales.

{pony_northern_european}The Prancing Pony
{pony_northern_european_desc}The Prancing Pony is a meeting place for both Bree-folk and travellers on the Great East Road and the Greenway. The inn is a place to hear news of the outside worlds and is frequented by Men, Hobbits, Dwarves, and the occasional Wizard. The art of smoking pipe-weed is said to have begun in Bree and from the Prancing Pony it spread among the races of Middle-earth. The inn is also noted for its fine beer. \n\nIt is located on the Great East Road at the base of Bree-hill. The front of the inn faces the Road and an archway leads to a courtyard between two wings that runs back into the hill. The main door is to the left of the archway. A sign hangs over the door with a painting of a rearing pony and the words The Prancing Pony by Barliman Butterbur. Inside there is a large Common Room, several private parlours, and a number of bedrooms, including a few rooms in the north wing designed for Hobbits that are low to the ground and have round windows. The inn also had stables.

{tirith_aear}The Tirith Aear
{tirith_aear_desc}DO NOT TRANSLATE
{tirith_aear_desc_short}DO NOT TRANSLATE
{tirith_aear_northern_european}The Tirith Aear
{tirith_aear_northern_european_desc}The Tirith Aear, literally translated as 'Sea Guard' but known as 'Seaward', is a tall and proud tower constructed in the Castle-city of Dol Amroth to serve as a beacon of strength to all those who look upon it. Although tall, gleaming white and visible for miles around, the tower did not act as a lighthouse but rather as a bell tower, chiming to mark day to day business of Dol Amroth or in appreciation of grand events such as the marriages of two daughters of the city; Finduilas to Steward Denethor II and Lothíriel to Eomer, King of the Mark. The origin of the tower is unknown but many suggest it was constructed so that should Lord Amroth ever return to shore he would have a guide by which to do so.
{tirith_aear_northern_european_desc_short}The Tirith Aear is a mighty tower constructed in the Castle-city of Dol Amroth.

{amon_sul}The Watchtower of Amon Sûl
{amon_sul_desc}DO NOT TRANSLATE
{amon_sul_desc_short}DO NOT TRANSLATE
{amon_sul_northern_european}The Watchtower of Amon Sûl
{amon_sul_northern_european_desc}The Watchtower of Amon Sûl was built in the days of Elendil at the dawn of the Third Age and was constructed atop the strategically important hill know as Weathertop in westron and Amon Sûl in Sindarin (literally 'windy hill'). Weathertop lies at the southernmost tip of the Weather Hills and is the highest peak for miles around and it was there that the Palantir of the north was given a home; further adding to the strategic importance of the tower atop the hill. Upon Arnor's divide after the passing of King Eärendur, the hill was fiercely contested diplomatically as it stands at the intersection of three realms; Arthedain, Cardolan and Rhudaur, however the hill passed into the control of Arthedain and developed strong ties with the northern third of old Arnor. In the reign of Argeleb, when the Witch-king began to grow in power and the men of Rhudaur openly contested their brothers, the tower was strengthened and became a mighty bastion against the oncoming tide of evil from the north-east, providing the headquarters of a strong line the Dúnedain set up across the Weather Hills. Amon Sûl held out for nigh on half a century but was eventually overcome by the Witch-king whereupon Arveleg, son of Argeleb, was slain. The tower was then abandoned for many years but now, as the Dúnedain continue their tireless mission of protecting Eriador, it has become a prominent staging ground for the shadowy individuals hosting many armed men of the Dúnedain 'army' and calling men from all three realms of the past.
{amon_sul_northern_european_desc_short}The Watchtower of Amon Sûl was a mighty tower constructed in the glory days of Arnor but now sits in ruin.

In the reign of Argeleb, when the Witch-king began to grow in power and the men of Rhudaur openly contested their brothers, the tower was strengthened and became a mighty bastion against the oncoming tide of evil from the north-east, providing the headquarters of a strong line the Dúnedain set up across the Weather Hills. Amon Sûl held out for nigh on half a century but was eventually overcome by the Witch-king whereupon Arveleg, son of Argeleb, was slain. The tower was then abandoned for many years but now, as the Dúnedain continue their tireless mission of protecting Eriador, it has become a prominent staging ground for the shadowy individuals hosting many armed men of the Dúnedain 'army' and calling men from all three realms of the past.
{amon_sul_southern_european_desc_short}The Watchtower of Amon Sûl was a mighty tower constructed in the glory days of Arnor but now sits in ruin.

{hobbit_desc_short}DO NOT TRANSLATE
{hobbit_northern_european}Smials
{hobbit_northern_european_desc}Smials are hole dwellings used by Hobbits. They are composed of a tunnel or tunnels and rooms dug into the ground. Hills and banks are the most suitable locations for smials. \n\nThe tunnels of a smial are generally tube-shaped with round doors and round windows. The simplest smials have dirt walls and floors, while the better smials have panelled walls and tiled floors. Some smials are very small, while others have several branches and rooms. Brandy Hall and the Great Smials are mansions with numerous tunnels and rooms where many members of an extended family live. Bag End is an example of a large, single-family smial that has many rooms on either side of one main tunnel. \n\nHobbits have lived in smials for as far back as they could remember. The people of Rohan remember legends from when they lived in the North of the Halflings who lived in holes in sand dunes. After the Hobbits settled in the Shire, the custom of building smials remained, but Hobbits also began to build houses and other buildings above ground. By the end of the Third Age, it was generally the poorest and richest Hobbits who still dwelled in smials.
{hobbit_northern_european_desc_short}Hole dwellings used by Hobbits.

{office_northern_european}Office of the Mayor of Michel Delving
{office_northern_european_desc}The office of the Mayor is an ancient building, by Hobbit standards, that acts as both a popular inn and Mayoral seat of power. Originally used as simply a hall for the Mayor to house his guests when they came to speak with him, it quickly grew into a famous inn as his 'guests' would often stay for weeks. As such it has become the very centre of Michel Delving with all manner of news, and travellers, to make their way through its four walls. Whilst not being as well known as the Green Dragon or the Prancing Pony it is nevertheless an establishment held in high regard! Occasionally the Mayor does hold official gatherings here but as his power slowly passes to the thain the Office is used more and more as an inn than a grand hall.

{KD_Unity_Hall_southern_european}Hall of the Seven
{KD_Unity_Hall_southern_european_desc}With the successful reclamation of Moria, plans can be drawn up for a great gathering hall that will play host to representatives of all 7 clans of the Dwarves. From time to time, our brothers from Ered Luin, Erebor, the Iron Hills and the Orocarni will answer our call to arms and use the hall as their barracks. It is wise to construct the hall now that pilgrims and immigrants will make their way here from our sister cities.

{chamber_northern_european}The Chamber of Mazarbul
{chamber_northern_european_desc}Chamber of Records in Khazad-dûm. The Chamber of Mazarbul is located on the Seventh Level of Khazad-dûm, six levels above the East-gate. It is north of the Twenty-first Hall on the right-hand or east side of the corridor. The main entrance from the corridor is a stone door on hinges. \n\nThe Chamber of Mazarbul is a large square room. There is a window shaft high in the eastern wall and below it is a second door leading to a downward staircase. Records were kept in wooden iron-bound chests that were set in recesses in the walls. \n\nWhen Balin came to reclaim Khazad-dûm in 2989, he set up his seat in the Chamber of Mazarbul and the Dwarves lived in the Twenty-first Hall nearby. The Dwarves kept a record of their expedition which was known as the Book of Mazarbul.

{moon_northern_european}Tower of the Moon
{moon_northern_european_desc}Minas Ithil and Minas Anor were the twin guardians of Gondor's glorious capital at Osgiliath. Named for the moon and sun respectively they stood watch on either side of the river city. However, when Minas Ithil fell, the capital was moved to Minas Anor which was named anew as Minas Tirith or Tower of Guard. Its sister was also given a new name 'Minas Morgul', the Tower of Sorcery. Although it referred to the entire 'city' the name Tower of the Moon was also more specifically the name of the large tower at the settlements centre and subsequently it was this tower that spread the green hue over the walls of all Minas Morgul giving it its new more sinister name. The Tower stands tall still awaiting the return of its rightful masters and longing for the days that it can once again glow with a shimmering light rather than a darkening mist as it did in days gone by.

{barad}barad_dur
{barad_desc}DO NOT TRANSLATE
{barad_desc_short}DO NOT TRANSLATE
{barad_northern_european}Barad-dûr
{barad_northern_european_desc}Stronghold of Sauron in Mordor. The Dark Tower is at the end of a long spur of the Ash Mountains on the northern border of Mordor. The tower overlooks the plateau of Gorgoroth. A road leads north-west from the Dark Tower to the Black Gate, about 100 miles away. Mount Doom is about 30 miles directly west of the Dark Tower. Sauron's Road runs from the western gate of the Dark Tower over an iron bridge spanning an abyss and then across Gorgoroth to the eastern slopes of Mount Doom. \n\nThe Dark Tower is an immense fortress of immeasurable strength. It was made of iron and extremely hard stone and its gates are steel. The tower is black and it is wreathed in veils of shadow woven by Sauron. It is very tall with many walls, battlements, and towers. The highest tower is topped with an iron crown and in it is the Window of the Eye from which Sauron gazes. Within the Dark Tower are great courts and an armoury and windowless dungeons; and beneath the tower are deep pits. \n\nSauron began building the Dark Tower around the year 1000 of the Second Age, when he chose Mordor as his realm. The tower was completed around the year 1600 of the Second Age Sauron forged the One Ring in Mount Doom at this time as well, and the foundations of the Dark Tower were strengthened by the power of the Ring. \n\nSauron ruled from the Dark Tower and expanded his power in Middle-earth until he was challenged by Ar-Pharazôn, King of Númenor, in 3262 of the Second Age. Seeing the might of Ar-Pharazôn's forces, Sauron came down from the Dark Tower and allowed himself to be taken to Númenor. There he persuaded Ar-Pharazôn to defy the Valar and sail to the Undying Lands, which led to the Downfall of Númenor in 3319 of the Second Age \n\nSauron's physical body was lost in the destruction of Númenor, but his spirit returned to the Dark Tower in 3320 of the Second Age. There he took up the Ring again and assumed a new form. In the War of the Last Alliance, Elves and Men marched to war against Sauron and defeated his forces at the Battle of Dagorlad before the Black Gate in 3434 S.A. The armies of the Last Alliance then entered Mordor and besieged the Dark Tower. \n\nThe Siege of Barad-dûr lasted seven years. At last in 3441 of the Second Age, Sauron himself came down from his tower and fought with Gil-galad and Elendil. All three fell in that mortal contest and Isildur took the One Ring from Sauron and kept it for himself. The Dark Tower was destroyed, but the foundations could not be broken as long as the Ring survived. \n\nSauron returned around 1050 of the Third Age and established a new stronghold at Dol Guldur in Mirkwood. The White Council attacked Dol Guldur in 2941 and the next year Sauron returned in secret to Mordor. In 2951, he declared himself openly and began rebuilding the Dark Tower. Sauron has a palantír in the Dark Tower: most likely the Ithil-stone that had been taken by the Nazgûl from Minas Ithil.

The armies of the Last Alliance then entered Mordor and besieged the Dark Tower. \n\nThe Siege of Barad-dûr lasted seven years. At last in 3441 of the Second Age, Sauron himself came down from his tower and fought with Gil-galad and Elendil. All three fell in that mortal contest and Isildur took the One Ring from Sauron and kept it for himself. The Dark Tower was destroyed, but the foundations could not be broken as long as the Ring survived. \n\nSauron returned around 1050 of the Third Age and established a new stronghold at Dol Guldur in Mirkwood. The White Council attacked Dol Guldur in 2941 and the next year Sauron returned in secret to Mordor. In 2951, he declared himself openly and began rebuilding the Dark Tower. Sauron has a palantír in the Dark Tower: most likely the Ithil-stone that had been taken by the Nazgûl from Minas Ithil.
{barad_mesoamerican_desc_short}Sauron's stronghold of immeasurable strength.
{barad_middle_eastern_desc}Stronghold of Sauron in Mordor. The Dark Tower is at the end of a long spur of the Ash Mountains on the northern border of Mordor. The tower overlooks the plateau of Gorgoroth. A road leads north-west from the Dark Tower to the Black Gate, about 100 miles away. Mount Doom is about 30 miles directly west of the Dark Tower. Sauron's Road runs from the western gate of the Dark Tower over an iron bridge spanning an abyss and then across Gorgoroth to the eastern slopes of Mount Doom. \n\nThe Dark Tower is an immense fortress of immeasurable strength. It was made of iron and extremely hard stone and its gates are steel. The tower is black and it is wreathed in veils of shadow woven by Sauron. It is very tall with many walls, battlements, and towers. The highest tower is topped with an iron crown and in it is the Window of the Eye from which Sauron gazes. Within the Dark Tower are great courts and an armoury and windowless dungeons; and beneath the tower are deep pits. \n\nSauron began building the Dark Tower around the year 1000 of the Second Age, when he chose Mordor as his realm. The tower was completed around the year 1600 of the Second Age Sauron forged the One Ring in Mount Doom at this time as well, and the foundations of the Dark Tower were strengthened by the power of the Ring. \n\nSauron ruled from the Dark Tower and expanded his power in Middle-earth until he was challenged by Ar-Pharazôn, King of Númenor, in 3262 of the Second Age. Seeing the might of Ar-Pharazôn's forces, Sauron came down from the Dark Tower and allowed himself to be taken to Númenor. There he persuaded Ar-Pharazôn to defy the Valar and sail to the Undying Lands, which led to the Downfall of Númenor in 3319 of the Second Age \n\nSauron's physical body was lost in the destruction of Númenor, but his spirit returned to the Dark Tower in 3320 of the Second Age. There he took up the Ring again and assumed a new form. {gate}black_gate
{gate_desc}DO NOT TRANSLATE
{gate_desc_short}DO NOT TRANSLATE
{gate_northern_european}The Black Gate
{gate_northern_european_desc}Main entrance into Mordor. The Black Gate is located at the north-western corner of Mordor. It spans Cirith Gorgor, the Haunted Pass, at the point where the Ash Mountains met the Mountains of Shadow. Behind the Black Gate is the valley of Udûn which leads to the plain of Gorgoroth. \n\nThe Black Gate was made of iron set in a stone rampart that stretched between the high cliffs on either side of the pass. It had two great iron doors. There was a battlement across the top of the Black Gate which was patrolled by sentries. The Towers of the Teeth flanked the Black Gate: Narchost on the west, or right as one faced the Gate, and Carchost on the east or left. There were also hundreds of Orc-holes in the cliffs around the Black Gate. \n\nIn front of the Black Gate is the Desolation of the Morannon. It is a grim and barren land where nothing grows. There are mounds of blasted earth that leaks poisonous fumes. Two great Slag-hills face the Black Gate.  Mires and pools of mud and oily liquid stretch before the Black Gate like a moat. Beyond the Desolation of the Morannon is Dagorlad, the great Battle Plain. \n\nThree roads converge at the Black Gate. One road comes from the north across Dagorlad. Another came from the east alongside the Ash Mountains. This road is only about 50 miles long, extending just about to the point where Barad-dûr stands on the other side of the Ash Mountains. The third road is the Harad Road which runs southward from the Black Gate through Ithilien and on to the southern lands of Harad. \n\nIt was made by Sauron sometime after he chose Mordor as his realm in 1000 of the Second Age. In 3434, the War of the Last Alliance began with the Battle of Dagorlad on the plain in front of the Black Gate. The Men and Elves of the Last Alliance defeated Sauron's forces and assaulted the Black Gate. Sauron retreated to Barad-dûr and the Army of the Last Alliance managed to enter the Black Gate behind him. The Siege of Barad-dûr lasted seven years until 3441 when Sauron was finally defeated. \n\nSauron's spirit fled from Mordor into the East after the One Ring was taken from him. The Men of Gondor took control of the Black Gate and they built the Towers of the Teeth on either side of it. They kept watch over the Black Gate to guard against Sauron's return. \n\nThe watch on Mordor declined after the Great Plague of 1636 which killed many Men of Gondor, but the Black Gate remained under Gondor's control until at least 1944. In that year, King Ondoher of Gondor was slain in battle with the Wainriders in front of the Black Gate. The watch-towers of the Black Gate were abandoned by the Men of Gondor sometime afterwards - probably before 1980 when the Lord of the Nazgûl returned to Mordor.
{gate_northern_european_desc_short}Black Gate, the main entrance into Mordor.

The Men of Gondor took control of the Black Gate and they built the Towers of the Teeth on either side of it. They kept watch over the Black Gate to guard against Sauron's return. \n\nThe watch on Mordor declined after the Great Plague of 1636 which killed many Men of Gondor, but the Black Gate remained under Gondor's control until at least 1944. In that year, King Ondoher of Gondor was slain in battle with the Wainriders in front of the Black Gate. The watch-towers of the Black Gate were abandoned by the Men of Gondor sometime afterwards - probably before 1980 when the Lord of the Nazgûl returned to Mordor.
{gate_greek_desc_short}Black Gate, the main entrance into Mordor.
{gate_southern_european}The Black Gate
{gate_southern_european_desc}Main entrance into Mordor. The Black Gate is located at the north-western corner of Mordor. It spans Cirith Gorgor, the Haunted Pass, at the point where the Ash Mountains met the Mountains of Shadow. Behind the Black Gate is the valley of Udûn which leads to the plain of Gorgoroth. \n\nThe Black Gate was made of iron set in a stone rampart that stretched between the high cliffs on either side of the pass. It had two great iron doors. There was a battlement across the top of the Black Gate which was patrolled by sentries. The Towers of the Teeth flanked the Black Gate: Narchost on the west, or right as one faced the Gate, and Carchost on the east or left. There were also hundreds of Orc-holes in the cliffs around the Black Gate. \n\nIn front of the Black Gate is the Desolation of the Morannon. It is a grim and barren land where nothing grows. There are mounds of blasted earth that leaks poisonous fumes. Two great Slag-hills face the Black Gate.  Mires and pools of mud and oily liquid stretch before the Black Gate like a moat. Beyond the Desolation of the Morannon is Dagorlad, the great Battle Plain. \n\nThree roads converge at the Black Gate. One road comes from the north across Dagorlad. Another came from the east alongside the Ash Mountains. This road is only about 50 miles long, extending just about to the point where Barad-dûr stands on the other side of the Ash Mountains. The third road is the Harad Road which runs southward from the Black Gate through Ithilien and on to the southern lands of Harad. \n\nIt was made by Sauron sometime after he chose Mordor as his realm in 1000 of the Second Age. In 3434, the War of the Last Alliance began with the Battle of Dagorlad on the plain in front of the Black Gate. The Men and Elves of the Last Alliance defeated Sauron's forces and assaulted the Black Gate. Sauron retreated to Barad-dûr and the Army of the Last Alliance managed to enter the Black Gate behind him. The Siege of Barad-dûr lasted seven years until 3441 when Sauron was finally defeated. \n\nSauron's spirit fled from Mordor into the East after the One Ring was taken from him. The Men of Gondor took control of the Black Gate and they built the Towers of the Teeth on either side of it. They kept watch over the Black Gate to guard against Sauron's return. \n\nThe watch on Mordor declined after the Great Plague of 1636 which killed many Men of Gondor, but the Black Gate remained under Gondor's control until at least 1944. In that year, King Ondoher of Gondor was slain in battle with the Wainriders in front of the Black Gate. The watch-towers of the Black Gate were abandoned by the Men of Gondor sometime afterwards - probably before 1980 when the Lord of the Nazgûl returned to Mordor.

{teeth_northern_european}The Towers of the Teeth
{teeth_northern_european_desc}The Towers of the Teeth stand on either side of Cirith Gorgor, the Haunted Pass between the Mountains of Shadow and the Ash Mountains at the north-west corner of Mordor. Carchost is on the east (or left facing the Gate) and Narchost is on the west. The Black Gate bares the pass between the two towers. The towers are tall and strong and have window-holes that face north, east and west. \n\nThe Towers of the Teeth were built by the Men of Gondor after the defeat of Sauron in the War of the Last Alliance at the end of the Second Age in order to guard against the possibility of the Dark Lord's return to Mordor. The towers were still in the control of Gondor as late as 1944 of the Third Age, when King Ondoher of Gondor was slain in battle against the Wainriders before the Black Gate. The Towers of the Teeth were deserted at some point after that - probably before 1980 when the Lord of the Nazgûl returned to Mordor. \n\nIn 2942, Sauron returned to Mordor and the Towers of the Teeth came under his control. Sauron filled the towers with garrisons of armed guards who keeps ceaseless watch on the Black Gate.
{teeth_northern_european_desc_short}Watchtowers of the Black Gate

{hornburg}helms_deep
{hornburg_desc}DO NOT TRANSLATE
{hornburg_desc_short}DO NOT TRANSLATE
{hornburg_northern_european}The Hornburg
{hornburg_northern_european_desc}Helm's Deep is a narrow ravine with high cliffs on the northern and southern sides that block out the sunlight. The Deeping-wall is built across the entrance to the ravine, and at the northern end of the wall is the fortress of the Hornburg.  No enemy has ever captured the Hornburg while it was defended. \n\nThe Hornburg stands on a spur called the Hornrock that juts out from the northern cliff. It is surrounded by a wall, behind which is an outer court and a citadel containing an inner court and a tall tower. In the tower is the great horn of Helm Hammerhand. When the horn is sounded, it echoes throughout the ravine and causes fear and dismay among enemy forces. \n\nA causeway leads up to the Hornburg-gates. To one side of the main gate a narrow walkway leads along the edge of the Hornrock to a small postern-door into the Hornburg. There is also a rear-gate with a stairway leading down from the Hornburg into the ravine behind the Deeping-wall. \n\nThe Deeping-wall stands 20 feet high and is wide enough for four men to stand side by side. The surface of the wall is smooth and nearly seamless. There is a tall parapet on the wall with openings for archers. Three staircases lead down from the back of the wall into the ravine, and another staircase leads up into the Hornburg. \n\nBehind the Deeping-wall, the cliffs draw closer together and form the Narrows. At the far end of the Narrows is the entrance to the Glittering Caves under the Thrihyrne. The Deeping-stream flows from the caves and passes under the Deeping-wall through a small culvert and then loop around the Hornburg and under the causeway. From the Hornburg, the Deeping-road runs alongside the Deeping-stream to the Great West Road. \n\nThe fortress and the Deeping-wall were built by the Men of Gondor sometime during the reign of the Ship-kings (830-1149). Its purpose is to guard the southern side of the Gap, while Isengard guards the northern side.
{hornburg_northern_european_desc_short}The Hornburg is a stronghold that guards the southern end of the Gap of Rohan.

{hall_northern_european}Meduseld - The Golden Hall
{hall_northern_european_desc}The Golden Hall of the Kings of Rohan, also known as Meduseld sits atop the city of Edoras, the capital of Rohan at the foot of the White Mountains. Edoras was built on a hill and Meduseld was at the summit, standing apart from the other buildings on a high platform built upon a green terrace. \n\nIts thatched roof gleams golden in the sunlight and can been seen from afar. A long, broad stair leads up the green terrace to a wide paved area in front of the door. Guards sit on seats carved from stone on either side of the top step.  The doors face north and were made of wood carved with images of beasts and birds with jewelled eyes and golden claws. On either side of the doors stand pillars hewn from mighty trees carved with interlacing figures that are gilded and painted. \n\nThe interior of Meduseld is a single long room. The high roof is supported by pillars that were decorated with carvings and gold and other colours. There is a louvre in the roof that let out smoke and lets in light. Light also comes into the hall through slitted, unglazed windows under the eaves on the eastern side. \n\nOn the walls are woven cloths that depict scenes and figures from the history of the Rohirrim, including one of Eorl the Young mounted on Felarof riding to the Battle of the Field of Celebrant. There is a long hearth in the middle of the hall. At the south end of the hall facing the door is a dais with three steps. On the dais is the King's throne, which was a great gilded chair. \n\nMeduseld was built by Brego, son of Eorl and was completed in 2569. At the feast held to hallow the hall, Brego's son Baldor vowed to walk the Paths of the Dead. He never returned, and his father Brego died of grief a year later.
{hall_northern_european_desc_short}The Golden Hall is the hall of the Kings of Rohan.

{wulf_hall_edoras_northern_european}Wulf's Hall
{wulf_hall_edoras_northern_european_desc}In the year 2758 of the Third Age, Edoras fell to Wulf and his Dunlending forces. Thus, did Wulf become known as the Twofold King of both Dunland and Rohan. His reign was short lived, for after the Long Winter, in 2759, Wulf himself was slain within the Meduseld, as a result of a duel between the Dunlanding King and Helm’s successor and nephew, Fréaláf who led a raid upon Edoras under the cover of darkness. And the Dunlending forces fled back to Dunland, led by Wulf’s wife, Drüalphíen. Now they have returned, led by Wulf’s successors and seized what they consider to be theirs by right, and no secret raids or assassination attempts will dislodge them.\n\nThis hall is proof of that. Once known as the Meduseld, they have rechristened it as the Wulf’s Hall, in honour of the Twofold King. And they have torn down the tapestries of those who stole their land, burning them in honour of Wulf. Likewise, they have defaced and burned their carvings, and now work to replace both carvings and tapestries with their own, commemorating Wulf, Dunland and its heroes. Furthermore, it has been expanded and its once golden roof of straw has been replaced with a traditional Dunlending roof, adorned with carvings of crebain, showing clearly to all who see it that Wulf's line once again rules in Edoras. And perhaps most terrifyingly for Dunland’s foes, the vast armouries and stables of the Golden Hall has allowed them to equip an elite force of cavalry, the Wulfguard Champions, that embodies the best of both traditional Dunlending Dunhird tactics, and the modern cavalry tactics that Wulf brought to Dunland. 
{wulf_hall_edoras_northern_european_desc_short}Wulf's Hall

{elrond_house_northern_european}The Last Homely House
{elrond_house_northern_european_desc}Home of Elrond in Rivendell. It is not known precisely when the Last Homely House was built, but Elrond established his refuge in Rivendell in 1697 of the Second Age. In addition to Elrond and his family, a number of other Elves resided or visited there. Among these were the Elf-lord Glorfindel, Elrond's counsellor Erestor, and Lindir. Aragorn was raised in the Last Homely House from 2933 to 2951 of the Third Age, and he frequently returns to visit. \n\nThe Last Homely House is located in a deep, hidden valley. There is only one path leading to the house. It passes over a narrow stone bridge without a parapet that spans one of the swift-running mountain streams that forms the River Bruinen. \n\nThe house is large and has many rooms and halls. The main room is the Hall of Fire. It was so named because of the great hearth set between two carved pillars with a fire that blazed year-round. The Hall of Fire is usually a quiet place for people to sit and think, but on high days it is filled with stories and songs.

{hunting_camp_northern_european}Hunting Camp
{hunting_camp_northern_european_desc}The hunting camp is the home of the Woodland Hunters. The camp exists out of wooden cabins and tents placed at the edge of the wild. The cabins are mostly used to preserve the fresh meat from decaying and to store their tools. The tents have the sole purpose of being a sleeping quarter of the Woodland Hunters. While these men reside in the camp they learn the skills of a true hunter. With bow and arrow they hunt on the wild animals which live near the settlement and when necessary the Woodland Hunters will take up arms to attack any Orcs on their path. The addition of this food network and sleeping quarters allows the town that hosts the hunters to freely support more troops.
{hunting_camp_northern_european_desc_short}A Hunting Camp allows the recruitment of organized woodsmen.

{greek_history_greek}History Guild
{greek_history_greek_desc}The Ñoldor are the wise, the lore-masters, the crafters. They’re in love with nearly all skills of craft of the dominion of the Vala Aulë, but language and history are probably their most beloved subjects of lore. At all times, even during the wars against Morgoth in the First Age, their lore-masters invented new words. It was Rúmil of Tirion who first invented letters with which words could be written down. The Tengwar they were called by the Ñoldor. Fëanor enhanced, and for large parts invented anew, the system which was created by Rúmil. The Tengwar fëanorinwa are still popular all over Middle-earth and used these days. Accompanied with the invention of script, the Ñoldor began to keep track of the events of their time. They even recorded whatsoever account of history the Valar were willing to reveal to them.  The Gwaith-i-Lúmenquentalë (History Guild) is the centre of history-lore kept by the Ñoldor. Here their lore-masters discuss about events of the past and teach the willing tales of days long forgotten in the minds of Men. The amount of knowledge stored in the Gwaith-i-Lúmenquentalë is invaluable and so are the benefits of it.\n\nThe History Guild favours buildings for art, music and town halls. Only available in Grassland and Mountainous regions.
{greek_history_greek_desc_short}The History Guild slightly increases population growth.

{greek_dance_greek}Dance Guild
{greek_dance_greek_desc}All of the Quendi are in love with dancing and singing. It is said, that in the Eldar in Valinor preserved songs they used to sing beneath the stars at the shores of Cuiviénen and to which they used to dance. The Teleri was the clan of the Quendi from which the greatest singers came in the old days – save only Maglor, Fëanor son, who was obviously a Ñoldor. The Sindar and more so the Nandor who are of Teleri origin are no exemption to this. Even though their brothers, the Ñoldor, love singing and dancing as well and do preserve some of their greatest history in epic poems and tales, the Sindar and Nandor do this on a regular basis. One will seldom find a book of history amongst the Nandor and Sindar, but always will find songs of wisdom and nearly every account of history, which are performed with or without dance. The Gwaith-i-Glinadir'a'mereth is the place where the greatest singers and best performers of the Sindar and Nandor of the Realm of Thranduil come together for exchange, pleasure and celebrations. Wherever a Gwaith-i-Glinadir'a'mereth (Dance Guild) exists, it is the centre of culture not only on days of joy and celebration but in day-to-day Life.\n\nThe Dance Guild favours buildings for art, nature, music and entertainment.

When the Kingdom splintered, the House of Kings in Fornost became the new seat of Royal power and the insignia of Elendil's reign were kept in this grand palace for many years. When the city fell, the place was deserted and Elendil’s heirs went into hiding; bringing the signs of their power to the safety of Rivendell. The Dúnedain dwindled and the lesser men began to forget the kingdom of old except in their legends. But it seems that ancient legends and dreams have come to new life, as a king from the true lineage has indeed returned and is holding the sceptre of the realm in his firm hand. Arnor, for many centuries not more than a name, is about to become a reality again. The House of Kings has been rebuilt and from near and far the king is calling together his peoples so that they may pledge their allegiance and be rewarded for their loyalty – and see with their own eyes, that the kingdom is real.

When its master looks in it, he can communicate with other Stones and anyone who might be looking into them.\n\nThose men who are not of Númenórean descent or have long forgotten the majesty and power of Númenor will not see the Palantir for its true value and will simply use the mighty stone to gather more money for their cause.\n\nUnder the control of the Orcs, the Palantir is put to work to steal secrets from the men of Gondor and the Elves, this knowledge is then turned to their advantage and used to improve their poor weapons and refit their warriors faster.\n\nHaving known of the power Palantir for many years and keeping one under their control in Elostirion, the Elves turn this power to communicate with their brethren all over Middle-earth and help one another in their attempts to leave or fight, as such, the Elf lord governing a Palantir will certainly have the ability to improve his warriors in battle.\n\nThe Dwarves are industrious and knowing not the true potential of this fascinating stone they look inward and use the sight of the Palantir to find the most profitable veins in the earth. With the greater output in their mining endeavours, the Dwarves are able to reduce the cost of all of their stone-works, not just at the location of the Palantir but globally!\n\nHaving worked with the Seeing Stones for hundreds of years, the descendants of Númenor can use these mighty tools as more than just glorified spies. They can turn the power of their ancestors into improving all of their warriors against the power of evil.
{ithil_palantir_northern_european_desc_short}The Ithil-stone is Sauron's Palantír kept at Barad-dûr.

{teleri_barracks}teleri_barracks
{teleri_barracks_desc}DO NOT TRANSLATE
{teleri_barracks_desc_short}DO NOT TRANSLATE
{teleri_barracks_greek}Teleri Barracks
{teleri_barracks_greek_desc}The Teleri Barracks is a simple structure that provides a dedicated space for training and accommodation of the various Lindar warriors of the Eldar. Unlike the Ñoldor and Silvan Elves, the hearts of the Teleri yearn always for the sea and if they must be sent from home in times of war, then they will only settle by major water courses. Accordingly, the Teleri Barracks can only be built on the shores of the sea, on the shores of the lakes and on the banks of the following rivers:\n\nBrandywine, Bruinen, Gwathló, Carnen, Anduin, Isen, Lhûn, Harnen, Poros, Celduin and Entwash\n\nLindar battalions train faster in grasslands.
{teleri_barracks_greek_desc_short}The Teleri Barracks provides training of Lindar battalions.

The region of Rhudaur was the smallest of the successor states of Arnor, and the first to be corrupted by the influence of the Witch-king of Angmar. In secret, evil chieftains allied themselves with Angmar and began to rally many of the poor and filthy hillmen to their cause. They aroused the hatred these men felt for the proud and rich 'pure blooded' Númenóreans of Arthedain and Cardolan. The hillmen had no major cities and the Dúnedain only built castles along the banks of the Hoarwell leaving many Rhudaurians to live in huts, tents and small villages. The evil of Angmar used this to their advantage and as such those who did not side with the Witch-king were easily caste out or cut down. After the fall of Angmar in T.A 1975, the population of Rhudaur dwindled owing primarily to the coming of Hill-trolls from the Ettenmoors. the land was slowly forgotten as 'Rhudaur' and came to be known as the Trollshaws and a bloody black and forth between the Dúnedain and the Trolls dominated the area's history for the remainder of the Third Age. {clan_fylani_northern_european_desc}Although the Seven Clans of Enedwaith may rule in unison from the Clan Moot at Alfcud, aided by the guidance of the Dubhsìthe, each Clan has their own Clanseat elsewhere that is their ancestral home and centre of power. This region holds one such Clanseat.\n\nThis Clanseat is the ancestral home of the Fylani Clan. One of the newest of the clans, they are now spread out among the northern plains of Enedwaith. Once they dwelled on the plains of the Gap of Rohan, but when Wulf’s ruthless campaign of conquest reached them, they were singled out by the warlord for their ties to Rohan, and so they petitioned the Clanmoot for sanctuary, offering horses and chariots in exchange for new lands and a formal seat on the Moot. Among their ancestors, they count not only clansmen of Enedwaith and Dunland, but even the Men of the Mountains, and they once married folk of Rohan and Gondor. Their heritage reflects this mixed blood, and they are innovators and capable horseback riders and were responsible for reintroducing both chariots and organized cavalry to the clans. Although the elder clans may label them as mongrels, it is in this mixed blood they have found their identity. Their symbol of two astride scarlet stallions reflects their pride in cavalry. Once secured, this Clanseat can muster the Fylani.

{clan_faolan_northern_european}Seat of the Faolan
{clan_faolan_northern_european_desc}Although the Seven Clans of Enedwaith may rule in unison from the Clan Moot at Alfcud, aided by the guidance of the Dubhsìthe, each Clan has their own Clanseat elsewhere that is their ancestral home and centre of power. This region holds one such Clanseat.\n\nThis Clanseat is the ancestral home of the Faolan Clan. Like the Fylani, they are a fairly young clan, arising from men of Dunland who abandoned their lands following Wulf’s savage consolidation of power that forged the clans of Dunland into a more united host- disagreeing with this, and wishing to preserve their heritage, the Faolan turned coat and pledged their loyalty to the Moot instead. They keep many of the old traditions of Dunland alive, being fierce tattooed warriors and strong drinkers, and hold the strong keep of Heorot. Like the Mocháini, they are settled and survive through raids upon Dunland, and the generosity of other clans that donate supplies in exchange for the Faolan’s efforts in defending Enedwaith from Dunland. Their name is apt for it means wolf, and the Faolan are wolves who prowl among the lands of their former kin. Their emblem is a sword upon a hill, representing their skill with the blade, and their keep of Heorot. Once secured, this Clanseat can muster the Faolan.

{clan_dubhshith_northern_european}Great Circle of the Dubhsìthe
{clan_dubhshith_northern_european_desc}The Great Circle of Eryn Vorn stands in the centre of what remains of the Great Forest and is the ancestral stronghold of the Dubhsìthe, the Black Stalkers of Peace. A people steeped in mystery, they dwell far from the Moot and the lands of the clans surrounding it and are said to be sworn to the forest itself rather than any symbol or leader. Certainly, this is true for they have come to act as enforcers of neutrality between clans, settling disputes and lending guidance in the name of the Great Forest. Although some are born into their order, most join by forsaking their own clan and swearing their life to the Great Forest- a oath that can only be ended by death.\n\nLegends speak that the order was originally founded by refugees of the House of Haleth who fled to Enedwaith after the War of Wrath and that some of the order are their descendants. There may be some truth in this for like the Second House of Edain, they are secretive, bear few children and allow women to fight on the field of battle. They support the clans through ritual chanting, and when needed can move through the shadows and deliver poison filled javelins and arrows to the foe. Once secured, the Great Cirlce can muster the Dubhsìthe. 
{clan_dubhshith_northern_european_desc_short}Great Circle of the Dubhsìthe

{clan_lond_northern_european}Seat of the Báirseach
{clan_lond_northern_european_desc}Although the Seven Clans of Enedwaith may rule in unison from the Clan Moot at Alfcud, aided by the guidance of the Dubhsìthe, each Clan has their own Clanseat elsewhere that is their ancestral home and centre of power. This region holds one such Clanseat.\n\nThis Clanseat is the ancestral home of the Báirseach Clan. Although their southern seat and settled nature may lead one to conclude they are a young clan, they are one of the eldest. It is said they survived the Great Logging as they betrayed their own kin and traded lumber for the knowledge of ship building, which allowed them to develop the feared Dragon Boats. Soon they realized however that they were being used by Númenor and aided the clans in leading a rebellion, by mounting swift naval attacks. This courage redeemed themselves in their kin’s eyes, and they reclaimed their seat on the Moot, although some have distrusted them ever since. Since then, they have plied their way as traders and mercenaries, cultivating ties with Gondor, the Drúedain and even far off Lindon and Ered Luin, while also offering their naval might to the Moot when it requires it. Their name appropriately has a dual meaning, reflecting their heritage as traders and sea warriors, translating as both bargain and dragon and it is this sea dragon that acts as their emblem. Once secured, this Clanseat can muster the Báirseach. 
{clan_lond_northern_european_desc_short}Seat of the Báirseach

{clan_tharbad_desc_short}DO NOT TRANSLATE 
{clan_tharbad_northern_european}Tír Croícoill 
{clan_tharbad_northern_european_desc}What has stood out most to everyone who enters Athámor is the Tír Croícoill, the heart of the forest, a gilded marbled hall that stands within the heart of the city. Acting as the seat of the Ruling Council of Athámor, it is where foreign diplomats are entertained, and pacts signed. At first, they often scoff at the structure, finding it hard to believe that the people they long believed to be wildmen constructed it. And yet built by them it was, for in truth they did not lack skill, a fact evident by their skilled and beautiful carvings of wood and stone, but materials and motivation. The reclaimation of Athámor provided both of the latter, with their love of their new nation and their restored capital leading them all, but especially the Mocháini, whom are most skilled in construction, to excel.\n\nThe original Tír Croícoill  was said to have stood in a glade in the center of the Great Forest, fashioned from living trees with a roof of leaves. It was burnt and the ground beneath it salted by the Númenóreans as a statement to what would happen to those who resisted their attempts to 'enlighten' them, and they constructed Tharbad over it, and the capital Athámor that it stood within. They did not seek to rebuild this hall, for it is forever lost, but fashion a new one in the spirit of the old. Its gilded spires echo the sun's reflections on the leaves of the forest, its carved pillars stand firm like the trunks of eld, displaying the stories and traditions of each clan, and its marble shows that the hall is the equal to any foreign palace. Any dignitary soon loses any pretensions of superiority if they wish to seriously treat with the Ruling Council, and cannot resist being awed by this impressive hall. Additionally, it also acts as a mustering ground for the new elite forces, which can meet almost any other foreign human force on equal grounds, and this uniformed force also often impresses the same foreign diplomats. \n\nIt truly shows that the Clans of Enedwaith are now the equal to any other nation and have come very far from the days of them being bickering clans. At last they have risen from the shadows of obscurity into the dawn of a new era!
{clan_tharbad_northern_european_desc_short}A gilded marbled hall that acts as the seat of the Ruling Council of Athámor.
